Hi Samir — thanks for flagging this.

Short answer: we ran a retroactive capacity reconciliation when we finalized March utilization across committed pools and it produced a one-time true-up line. I’ve attached the per-model/per-region usage CSV (usage_report_Mar2026.csv) and included a short explanation below.

What happened (high level):
- During March you hit short bursts across two dedicated pools (us-west and us-east) that exhausted reserved slots; the serving runtime then routed some bursts to on-demand variants which are billed at our overage rate.
- The reconciliation compares committed units in the signed SOW to actual consumed capacity across model variants and converts the delta into a one-time true-up charge.

Attachment: usage_report_Mar2026.csv (per-model rows, hourly buckets, region tags)
SOW reference: SOW v3 (signed 2025-11-03) — section 4.2 (Capacity reconciliation and true-up). I can attach the signed SOW on request.

Options we can offer:
1) Issue an amended invoice that splits the one-time true-up into two equal line items across April and May (no finance fees).
2) Apply a one-time courtesy credit equal to 10% of the true-up amount in recognition of the system behavior during a portion of the month while we tuned routing.
3) If you prefer, we can keep the invoice as-is and issue a credit memo once you approve the reconciliation.

Tell me which you prefer and I’ll coordinate with Rishi on the accounting-side and Marissa on contract/SOW references. If you’d like a short call to walk through the CSV, we can do 30 minutes today.

Best,
